headline_marked: Parliament [[passes law to replace RAB with SRB]], opposition slams move
headline: Parliament passes law to replace RAB with SRB, opposition slams move
summary: The government has abolished the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and established the Special Response Battalion (SRB), though critics call it 'old wine in a new bottle'.
details: The Bangladesh Parliament has passed the Special Response Battalion (SRB) Bill 2026, officially abolishing the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and establishing a new specialised police unit.
RAB, formed in 2003, had faced widespread international criticism and US sanctions over serious human rights violations, including enforced disappearances.
The new law transfers RAB's personnel, offices, powers, records, assets, and liabilities directly to the SRB, a move the government says preserves state resources.
Opposition members, including those from BNP and Jamaat, strongly objected, arguing that the SRB is merely a reorganised RAB under a different name.
Leader of the Opposition Shafiqur Rahman stated that while the abolition of RAB was a universal demand, no one called for a replacement force mirroring its structure.
Jamaat MP Nurul Islam criticised the government for rushing the bill through parliament in four working days without adequate stakeholder consultation.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed defended the move, stating it fulfills a pledge to abolish RAB and prevents the waste of expensive intelligence gear and weaponry.
Opposition MPs further argued that transferring all assets and records to the SRB could leave past cases of enforced disappearances vulnerable to flawed investigations.
caption:
RAB is gone, but is the new SRB just the same force with a different name? Parliament passes the replacement bill amid fierce opposition.

The Bangladesh Parliament has passed the Special Response Battalion (SRB) Bill 2026, officially abolishing the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and establishing a new specialised police unit.

RAB, formed in 2003, had faced widespread international criticism and US sanctions over serious human rights violations, including enforced disappearances.

The new law transfers RAB's personnel, offices, powers, records, assets, and liabilities directly to the SRB, a move the government says preserves state resources.

Opposition members, including those from BNP and Jamaat, strongly objected, arguing that the SRB is merely a reorganised RAB under a different name.

Leader of the Opposition Shafiqur Rahman stated that while the abolition of RAB was a universal demand, no one called for a replacement force mirroring its structure.

Jamaat MP Nurul Islam criticised the government for rushing the bill through parliament in four working days without adequate stakeholder consultation.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed defended the move, stating it fulfills a pledge to abolish RAB and prevents the waste of expensive intelligence gear and weaponry.

Opposition MPs further argued that transferring all assets and records to the SRB could leave past cases of enforced disappearances vulnerable to flawed investigations.

headline: 6 deaths in 24 hours: Dengue claims 6 more lives as 1,492 are hospitalised
summary: The daily death toll marks the second highest of the year, with total fatalities reaching 139 and cases climbing to 48,430.
details: At least six dengue patients died and 1,492 others were hospitalised within a 24-hour period ending at 8:00am today.
The deaths were spread across several regions, with two reported in the Khulna division and one each in Barishal, Dhaka, Chattogram, and Rajshahi divisions.
This latest surge brings the total number of dengue deaths this year to 139, while the total number of cases has risen to 48,430.
Currently, 3,434 dengue patients are receiving treatment at various hospitals across the country.
